fixes.explanation: That's exactly it, friend. The text says the Philistines "…all went in search of him…" (2 Samuel 5:17). Not a few of them, ALL of them. They heard David had been anointed king over Israel, and the whole crowd came looking.

Not this one, friend. Pulling back isn't what the text says. When the Philistines heard David had been anointed king over Israel, they "…all went in search of him…" (2 Samuel 5:17). Backing off would be the quiet option, and this crowd wasn't feeling quiet.

Good guess, friend, but the text doesn't say they waited. When they heard David had been anointed king over Israel, they "…all went in search of him…" (2 Samuel 5:17). That's a crowd with their shoes already on.

That's the one, friend. The Philistines were spread out in the Valley of Rephaim, and "…David inquired of the LORD…" (2 Samuel 5:19). When the question was whether to go up against them, he took it straight to God. I know plenty of folks who ask LAST.

Reasonable thing to do, friend, but the text doesn't say he did it. It says "…David inquired of the LORD…" (2 Samuel 5:19). He asked God whether he should go up against the Philistines, not how many men he had.
Not so, friend, it's False. David didn't skip a step. The text says "…David inquired of the LORD…" again (2 Samuel 5:23). The earlier win didn't replace the new question.

Not quite, friend. The LORD gave David a plan with action in it: "…circle around behind them and attack them in front of the balsam trees." (2 Samuel 5:23). There's a sound to listen for in the treetops, and then the word is "move quickly" (2 Samuel 5:24). Nothing about waiting for the Philistines to leave.

Yes, friend. The text says, "So David did as the LORD had commanded him…" (2 Samuel 5:25). No tweaking and no shortcuts. That's following the recipe exactly, and my own stamping would have blurred half of it.
